cards.title: World Notes: Reindeer and Sledges
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read the chapters with your lens in mind.
text: Reindeer live in the cold far north, in places like Norway, Sweden and Finland.
For a very long time, people there have trained reindeer to pull sledges over the snow. A sledge is a sled.
In Chapter 3, the Queen’s sledge is pulled by two white reindeer with bells on their harness.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Last day of the week. Put it all together: what makes Narnia feel real, and how do you know?
transcripts.guide1: Word work: roll tele words, edit in passes, and roll for the lazy uh.
transcripts.guide2: Look back at Chapters 1 to 3 and pick your best detail.
transcripts.guide3: Today you finish your literary response with a closing sentence.

notes.wordParts: The word part tele means far. telephone = sound from far away. telescope = a tool for looking far away.
notes.grammar: A complex sentence has a main idea and a part that cannot stand alone, joined by a word like when, because or although. When that part comes first, put a comma after it.
notes.spelling: The schwa is a lazy uh sound in a quiet beat of a long word. Any vowel can make it: the a in sofa, the e in seven, the o in lemon.
notes.wgrd: A reader believes a fantasy world when the details feel real: what you can see, hear and touch.
vocab: eager to find out; very curious
a deep feeling of sadness or gloom
strange or unusual in a hard-to-explain way

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: When the Faun asks, Lucy tells him the truth: she is human.
Peter says Lucy’s story is “a jolly good hoax.”
items.why: Peter thinks Lucy made it up. He is wrong about her.

items.t: Lucy tells the others, “It’s a magic wardrobe. There’s a wood inside it.”
items.why: She tells them exactly what she saw.
